Counsel for Applicant :- Shikhar Awasthi Counsel for Opposite Party :- Dur Vijay Singh,G.A.,Kamal Kaushal Upadhyay Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
IInd
Supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken in the record.
Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of the second bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.574 of 2021 at Police Station-Sadar Bazar, District-Agra under Sections 498A, 307 IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 11.12.2021.
The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on 24.01.2024.

Niraj vs State Of U.P. on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171694957/
1

The following arguments made by Shri Shikhar Awasthi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Dur Vijay Singh, learned counsel for the informant and Shri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is a law abiding citizen who cooperated in the investigation and has joined the trial proceedings.
The applicant never tampered with the evidence nor did he influence any witness.
2. The applicant did not adopt dilatory tactics or impede the progress of the trial in any manner.
3. The status report sent by the learned trial court records that the prosecution proposes to examine 5 witnesses to bring home the charges.
However, three prosecution witnesses including the material witnesses have been examined till date.
4. The prosecution evidence is close to the conclusion.
Thereafter, the stage is set for the defence evidence.

5. Continued incarceration of the applicant will disable him from framing an effective defence strategy and prevent him from gathering evidence in his support thereof and tendering the same before the learned trial court to establish his innocence.

sentences.text: The Court has also to factor the likelihood of whether the accused committed the offence while deciding a bail application.

The court also has to determine in the facts of the case whether the accused needs to be set at liberty to frame his defence and gather evidence to refute the prosecution case and establish his innocence.
The bail court has to examine whether continued incarceration would disable the accused from tendering an effective defence of his case.
This is a demand of processual fairness in criminal jurisprudence.
Setting an accused at liberty at large on this ground cannot be applied mechanically in all cases.
The issue has to be considered in the facts and circumstances of each case while doing so.
All relevant facts including the evidences in the record, the conduct of the accused during the investigation as well as trial have to be adverted to before a decision is made in this regard."
Considering the aforesaid parameters in light of the above facts of this case, I am of the opinion that Prabhat Gangwar (supra) is applicable to the facts of this case.

Niraj vs State Of U.P. on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171694957/
2 6.
The applicant has explained his criminal history.
It is also contended that the applicant is a convenient scapegoat for the police authorities who nominated him in another false criminal case to burnish their professional credentials.
The said case does not have any bearing on the instant bail application.
7. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of the applicant influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant-Niraj be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
